recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. The current core source satisfies the FHIR-20511 resolution; future concerns about broader participant wording should be handled as a separate editorial tracker because the conformance target profiles and actor element wording already convey the machine-as-Device rule.
issue_request: FHIR-20511 was a Published PA change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked how to model AI or other machine interactions that resemble encounters; the accepted resolution was to add Device to the Encounter.participant.individual reference choices and rename Encounter.participant.individual to Encounter.participant.actor for consistency with Appointment.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-20511 was found. The source effect appears to have been applied through overlapping FHIR-22696 work: commit 21e95de9dcd529dbd870ecff97c456cee1ae6309 added Device and HealthcareService to Encounter.participant.individual, and commit d1af9f83a1fba890f97ff6d9c02af936d77bb836 renamed the element to Encounter.participant.actor while updating Encounter participant search parameters.
additional_context: FHIR-22696's Published resolution explicitly listed Encounter.participant.actor as Reference(Patient | Group | Practitioner | PractitionerRole | RelatedPerson | Device | HealthcareService), matching the current source. The Zulip thread that led to FHIR-20511 recommended extending Encounter.participant with Device. Later FHIR-35810 Practitioner guidance confirms that autonomous systems and machines, including AI/ML systems, should be represented with Device rather than Practitioner. Confluence searches found no FHIR-20511 decision record that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Encounter is active in source/fhir.ini, the current Encounter StructureDefinition defines Encounter.participant.actor with Device among its Reference target profiles, and the Encounter participant search parameters use Encounter.participant.actor rather than the old individual path.
